subject: Ophthalmology
content: Ophthalmology focuses on the anatomy, physiology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of disorders of the eye and visual system.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Vision depends on coordinated function of the eye, optic nerve, visual pathways, and visual areas of the brain.
source: NCBI Bookshelf - Anatomy, Head and Neck, Eye

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The major structures of the eye include the cornea, sclera, iris, lens, ciliary body, retina, choroid, optic nerve, and associated muscles.
source: NCBI Bookshelf - Anatomy, Head and Neck, Eye

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The cornea is the transparent anterior surface of the eye and provides a major part of the eye's refractive power.
source: NCBI Bookshelf - Anatomy, Head and Neck, Eye
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The crystalline lens focuses light onto the retina and changes shape during accommodation to support near vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The retina contains photoreceptor and neural cells that convert light into electrical signals transmitted toward the brain through the optic nerve.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The optic nerve carries visual information from the retina toward the brain and is essential for normal vision.
source: NCBI Bookshelf - Anatomy, Head and Neck, Eye
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Accommodation changes the refractive power of the eye to focus on objects at different distances, particularly near objects.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: The pupillary light reflex changes pupil size in response to light and involves retinal, midbrain, and autonomic pathways.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Intraocular pressure is determined by the balance between aqueous humor production and drainage and is clinically important in glaucoma.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Myopia occurs when the eye focuses distant images in front of the retina, resulting in blurred distance vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Hyperopia is a refractive error in which the optical system tends to focus images behind the retina when accommodation is relaxed.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Astigmatism results from unequal curvature of the cornea or lens and can cause blurred or distorted vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Presbyopia is age-related reduction in the eye's ability to accommodate for near vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Refractive errors can often be corrected with spectacles, contact lenses, or selected refractive procedures depending on the individual.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: A cataract is clouding of the eye's natural lens that can reduce vision and may progress over time.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Cataract can cause blurred vision, glare, reduced contrast, difficulty seeing at night, and changes in refractive prescription.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Cataract surgery removes the cloudy natural lens and generally replaces it with an artificial intraocular lens.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can damage the optic nerve and cause irreversible vision loss if untreated.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Open-angle glaucoma develops gradually and may cause peripheral visual field loss before a person notices symptoms.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Angle-closure glaucoma occurs when the drainage angle becomes blocked and can cause a rapid rise in intraocular pressure.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Evaluation for glaucoma may include measurement of intraocular pressure, optic nerve examination, visual field testing, and assessment of the anterior chamber angle.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Diabetic retinopathy is retinal damage caused by diabetes-related blood vessel abnormalities and can lead to vision loss.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Diabetic macular edema occurs when fluid accumulates in the macula as a result of diabetic retinal vascular damage and can impair central vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Age-related macular degeneration affects the macula and can impair central vision, particularly in older adults.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Dry age-related macular degeneration involves degeneration of macular retinal tissues and may progress gradually with loss of central vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Wet age-related macular degeneration involves abnormal blood vessel growth beneath or within the retina and can cause rapid central vision loss.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Retinal detachment occurs when the retina separates from its supporting tissues and can cause permanent vision loss without timely treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Retinal vein or artery occlusion can impair retinal blood flow and cause sudden or progressive visual loss.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Optic neuritis is inflammation or demyelinating injury of the optic nerve and commonly causes painful loss of vision in one eye.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Optic neuropathy refers to dysfunction or damage of the optic nerve from causes including ischemia, inflammation, compression, toxins, or trauma.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Papilledema is swelling of the optic disc caused by raised intracranial pressure and requires urgent evaluation of the underlying cause.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Visual field defects can localize disease to the retina, optic nerve, chiasm, optic tract, radiations, or visual cortex.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Keratitis is inflammation or infection of the cornea and may cause pain, redness, photophobia, tearing, and reduced vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: A corneal ulcer is an open lesion of the cornea, often associated with infection, and can threaten vision if not treated promptly.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Keratoconus is progressive thinning and bulging of the cornea that can cause irregular astigmatism and impaired vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva and can be caused by infections, allergies, irritants, or other conditions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Allergic conjunctivitis results from an immune response to allergens and commonly causes itching, redness, and tearing.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Dry eye disease occurs when tears do not adequately lubricate and protect the ocular surface, causing discomfort and visual disturbance.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Blepharitis is inflammation of the eyelid margins and can cause irritation, crusting, redness, and ocular surface symptoms.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: A chalazion is a localized eyelid lump caused by blockage and inflammation of a meibomian gland.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: A hordeolum is an acute localized infection or inflammation involving an eyelid gland and commonly appears as a tender eyelid swelling.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Anterior uveitis is inflammation of the anterior uveal tract and commonly presents with eye pain, photophobia, redness, and reduced vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Posterior uveitis affects the retina, choroid, or adjacent structures and may cause floaters or visual loss.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Trachoma is a chronic infectious eye disease caused by Chlamydia trachomatis and remains an important preventable cause of blindness in some populations.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Herpes simplex virus can infect the cornea and cause recurrent keratitis that may scar the cornea and impair vision.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Amblyopia is reduced vision caused by abnormal visual development during childhood and is associated with conditions such as strabismus or unequal refractive error.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Strabismus is misalignment of the eyes and can interfere with normal binocular visual development in children.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Retinopathy of prematurity is abnormal retinal vascular development in premature infants and can cause retinal detachment and blindness in severe disease.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: A corneal abrasion is a superficial injury to the corneal epithelium and can cause pain, tearing, photophobia, and foreign-body sensation.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Chemical exposure to the eye can rapidly damage the ocular surface and requires immediate irrigation and urgent assessment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: An open globe injury is a full-thickness wound of the eye wall and is an ophthalmic emergency requiring urgent specialist management.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Acute angle closure can cause sudden severe eye pain, blurred vision, halos, headache, nausea, and markedly elevated intraocular pressure.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Sudden loss of vision can result from retinal, vascular, optic nerve, neurological, or ocular causes and requires urgent evaluation.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Endophthalmitis is severe intraocular inflammation, often infectious, that can rapidly threaten vision and requires urgent treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Visual acuity testing measures the ability to resolve visual detail and is a fundamental part of ophthalmic assessment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Slit-lamp examination uses focused illumination and magnification to examine the anterior eye and selected posterior structures.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Fundus examination allows direct assessment of the retina, optic disc, macula, and retinal vessels.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Optical coherence tomography produces cross-sectional images of retinal and other ocular structures and is useful for several retinal and optic nerve disorders.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Tonometry measures intraocular pressure and is an important component of glaucoma evaluation.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Visual field testing measures peripheral and central visual function and can detect patterns of loss associated with glaucoma and neuro-ophthalmic disease.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Corrective lenses change the optical power reaching the eye and can correct common refractive errors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Intravitreal medicines are injected into the vitreous cavity to deliver treatment directly to the eye for selected retinal and other disorders.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Laser photocoagulation uses focused laser energy to treat selected retinal abnormalities and is used in several retinal conditions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Glaucoma treatment aims to lower intraocular pressure and preserve optic nerve function using medicines, laser procedures, surgery, or combinations.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Cataract that significantly affects vision is commonly treated with surgical removal of the cloudy lens and implantation of an artificial lens.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Regular eye evaluation and good diabetes management can help detect diabetic retinal disease and reduce the risk of vision loss.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Protective eyewear, safe handling of chemicals and tools, and appropriate workplace or sports precautions can reduce preventable eye injuries.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Comprehensive eye examinations can detect refractive errors and eye diseases, sometimes before symptoms become noticeable.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Early identification of refractive error, strabismus, amblyopia, and other childhood eye disorders supports timely intervention during visual development.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Ophthalmology
content: Ophthalmic care integrates visual function, ocular examination, systemic disease, imaging, treatment risks, rehabilitation needs, and patient preferences.
